_comment: The wake-time slider on the Dynamic Scheduler case study: what the bot does when you send /awake. The day is planned from the wake time: the first task starts `lead` minutes later, then the blocks follow in order of priority, sized and ordered by how early or late the wake time is. Times are minutes after midnight unless written HH:MM. Per-zone values are [early, normal, late] and blend over the last `blend` minutes before each zone edge (so a zone is fully itself from its first minute), so blocks shrink, grow, fade and change places as the slider moves.
_lead: The first block always starts this many minutes after the wake time. The copy beside the slider prints this number.
_sweepMs: How long the opening sweep takes (07:00, 03:00, 15:00, back to 07:00).
_day: The waking day: 16 hours from the wake time, then the sleep block.
_fade: A block fades in or out over this many minutes of wake time, inside the ends of its show range.
_gap: Time no block claims becomes an Open time row once it is at least this long.
_bar: A duration bar is full at this many minutes.

zones.name: Early start
zones.line: A long workout first, time for a hobby and good habits, then focused work and a light early evening.

zones.name: Normal start
zones.line: Crucial tasks come first. Everything else shrinks or slides later, and the workout gets short.

zones.name: Late start
zones.line: A slow start, one focus block, then leisure, people and errands. Sleep lands the next morning.

_blocks: show: the wake-time range the block exists in. duration, priority: [early, normal, late]; the lowest priority goes first. anchor (optional; without one a block simply follows the block before it): wake = not before this many minutes after waking; clock = not before this time of day.
